newsitem.title: PERU: Freed hostages were two Peruvians, two Japanese.
newsitem.headline: Freed hostages were two Peruvians, two Japanese.

text.p: The four hostages released on Thursday night from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima were two Japanese and two Peruvians, Red Cross officials said.
The officials said the Japanese were businessmen and that one of the Peruvians was an official of the Japanese company Nissan. The fourth hostage's occupation was unknown.
On Wednesday the guerrrillas released ten men, including four diplomats who have since been acting as mediators in negotiations.
In the first hours after the assault late on Tuesday night, the rebels released about 80 women and elderly men.
The guerrillas have threatened to kill the hostages, who number up to 400.
